objective: Managing and escalating issues to appropriate decision-makers for timely resolution
secondaryObjectives: Collecting and consolidating key performance metrics defined by the portfolio governance model
Analyzing and optimizing resource allocation/reallocation (people, tools, technology, finance) via supply/demand analysis

sources.cite: PMI, Portfolio Management Professional (PfMP) Examination Content Outline (PRA-206-2017, July 2017): Strategic Alignment 25%, Governance 20%, Portfolio Performance 25%, Portfolio Risk Management 15%, Communications Management 15%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of a copy of PMI's PDF hosted by a training provider. Relevant text: Strategic Alignment Task 5 scenarios 'in order to evaluate and select viable options'; Task 6 'Recommend portfolio scenario(s) and related components, based on prioritization analysis/criteria'; Task 7 'Determine the impact to portfolio and portfolio components due to changes in strategic goals and objectives'; Portfolio Performance Task 6 'Balance portfolio and prioritize portfolio components, using established criteria and methods'; Task 7 'Analyze and optimize the consolidated allocation/reallocation of capacity'; Governance Task 5 'Make recommendations and obtain approval regarding portfolio decisions'. Whether PMI has a newer outline was not checked. The objective wording is the course seed's. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's pfmp-water-utility-rebalance (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The organization, the portfolio or program, the figures and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the portfolio manager for Harrowby Bank's change portfolio, a fictional bank: 24 components and 180 million dollars. The portfolio board meets fortnightly and decides on anything above the thresholds in the governance model.
handover: Governance model: issues affecting more than one component or more than 2 million dollars go to the portfolio board.
Each component reports its own metrics in its own format.
howItWorks: The board shows the risk register against the appetite, each stakeholder's support in words and the docket.
Move on a fortnight at a time. A decision comes to you at each board meeting; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Meeting 2: both contingencies run out; the board learns of the 4 million dollar overrun when the CFO's forecast breaks.
Meeting 3: the board funds a new initiative from a 'green' portfolio that is actually 6 million dollars over forecast.
Meeting 4: two component managers discover the moves from their burn-down; one escalates to the COO and the reallocation is reversed.

escPrompt.title: A 4 million dollar issue across two components
escPrompt.context: Both program managers want to handle it themselves.

choices.label: Escalate to the portfolio board with the impact on both components, options and a recommendation, as the governance model requires

effects.log: The board decides the vendor response.

choices.feedback: Issues above the thresholds or across components go to the level with authority, in time.

choices.label: Let the two managers try for a month, then escalate
choices.feedback: The board loses a month to act.

choices.label: Absorb it in the components' contingencies without telling the board
choices.feedback: A 4 million dollar cross-component issue is above your authority.

choices.label: Report the governance model's metrics consolidated across components (strategic contribution, SPI and CPI, benefits forecast, risk exposure) on one dashboard

effects.log: The board sees one consolidated view.

choices.feedback: Consolidated metrics show portfolio performance against strategy.

choices.label: Attach all 24 component reports
choices.feedback: The board can't see the portfolio as a whole.

choices.label: Show a red-amber-green list only
choices.feedback: Colors without figures hide the 4 million issue's effect on strategy.

resPrompt.title: Demand 140% of supply
resPrompt.context: Two low-priority components hold six engineers.

choices.label: Recommend moving four engineers from the two low-priority components to the strategic ones, with the schedule effect on each, for the board to approve
choices.feedback: Supply and demand analysis plus the prioritization model justify reallocation; the board approves it.

choices.label: Ask for budget to hire contractors
choices.feedback: It may help in months; priorities stay misaligned now.

choices.label: Move the engineers yourself without telling the component managers
choices.feedback: Moving people without the board or the managers breaks trust and plans.

scoring.modelReasoning: Portfolio performance management consolidates the governance model's metrics so the board sees the whole portfolio against strategy. Issues are escalated to the level with authority, as the thresholds say, in time to act. Resources are rebalanced from supply and demand analysis and the prioritization model, with the board's approval.
